analyst_view.overall: Early view: Sunderland (11th, 7 points) go in with a lift after beating Chelsea 1-0 to climb off the bottom of the Premier League, but Regis Le Bris has had a rough autumn and his side visit Aston Villa just before this. Granit Xhaka limped off after three minutes against Chelsea and the site lists Trai Hume as banned, while Jagiellonia (29th, 3 points) have lost three of four.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean lower: Sunderland have scored only four goals in four European games and their home games ended 1-0 and 0-2, while Jagiellonia's two away games were narrow defeats (1-2 at Olympiacos, 0-1 at Levski). A 1-0 or 2-0 home win fits better than a high score.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 7.3 of them for Sunderland. I lean lower: Sunderland had plenty of the ball against Dinamo but won few corners, which suggests they don't turn possession into corners as often as the numbers assume.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. Sunderland and Dinamo shared five bookings last time and Jagiellonia will need to break up play, but nothing points strongly away from about 4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.6 shots, 21.1 of them for Sunderland. I lean lower: Sunderland's attack has been blunt all autumn, Xhaka may be missing, and Le Bris has rotated heavily in Europe (four half-time changes against Dinamo), which is likely again after the Villa game.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. Sunderland forced seven saves from Dinamo's goalkeeper and Jagiellonia have conceded seven goals in four games, so I stay close to the number.
